_comment: Meteorological hazard thresholds used to create upstream hazard signals (flood potential, storm-force wind, dry spell, cold spell, low visibility). These are METEOROLOGICAL definitions, not health thresholds. Values with status 'existing_dashboard_design_unvalidated' are carried over from weather_script.js (renderRisks) so behaviour stays continuous; they are design choices, not evidence-based, and should be aligned with DMH practice. null = not configured.

heavy_rain_24h_mm.source: India Meteorological Department rainfall intensity category 'heavy rain' (64.5–115.5 mm in 24 h)

very_heavy_rain_24h_mm.source: India Meteorological Department rainfall intensity category 'very heavy rain' (115.6–204.4 mm in 24 h)
very_heavy_rain_24h_mm.used_for: flood_potential proxy (rainfall alone does not establish flooding)

flood_7day_forecast_mm.source: Existing dashboard rule in weather_script.js: 7-day forecast rain >= 200 mm = 'flood risk (high)'
flood_7day_forecast_mm.used_for: flood_potential proxy over the next 7 days

storm_force_wind_kmh.source: Beaufort scale force 10 (storm) lower bound, 24.5 m/s ≈ 89 km/h sustained wind
storm_force_wind_kmh.note: weather_script.js labels current wind >= 60 km/h as 'storm-force'; 60 km/h is in the Beaufort 7–8 (near gale/gale) range, so the engine keeps the Beaufort 10 value for this label.

dry_spell_min_consecutive_dry_days.source: Wet day = daily precipitation ≥ 1 mm (ETCCDI convention). Run length for a 'dry spell' is not set.

dry_spell_forecast.source: Existing dashboard rule in weather_script.js: 7-day forecast rain < 2 mm with temperature >= 32 °C

cold_spell_tmin_c.source: Existing dashboard rule in weather_script.js: temperature <= 10 °C (engine applies it to the daily minimum)

low_visibility_m.source: WMO definition of fog: horizontal visibility below 1 km
